physical_meaning: net longitudinal deceleration between TOR and the onset of effective human braking
powertrain_or_control_architecture: sum of drag, powertrain drag / lift-off regen, and any automation command
measurement_method: not a single measured quantity; decomposes into V02-V05 and transition rows T04/T08
reported_range: 0 (automation holds speed) to about 4 (strong lift-off regen or automation braking)
relevant_to_human_fallback: YES (largest model elasticity after v0 and a_max)
notes: Not an EV-vs-ICE property. Which component applies depends first on the transition policy (does automation keep control?) and only then on the powertrain. See report section 4.

physical_meaning: deceleration from rolling resistance, driveline in neutral and aerodynamic drag, no propulsion or braking
vehicle_type: light-duty vehicles, US certification fleet MY2024 (1,537 unique configurations)
powertrain_or_control_architecture: all powertrains (road-load only; regen and engine braking excluded)
measurement_method: EPA target coefficients A+Bv+Cv^2 divided by equivalent test weight (src/experiments/r3a_coastdown_epa.py)
reported_range: 100 km/h: median 0.31, 5-95% 0.22-0.40 (non-electric 0.32, BEV road-load 0.23); 130 km/h: median 0.46
relevant_to_human_fallback: YES (lower bound of a_pre when propulsion is released and nothing else acts)
notes: Speed-dependent. An order of magnitude below regen / automation deceleration: a_pre above ~0.5 m/s2 cannot come from drag alone.

phenomenon: ICE engine braking on accelerator release
physical_meaning: additional deceleration from engine pumping/friction when the accelerator is released in gear
powertrain_or_control_architecture: gear, transmission (manual / automatic / CVT coasting logic) and fuel cut-off dependent
reported_range: >= a_drag (V02); upper value not established from sources checked
relevant_to_human_fallback: YES (component of a_pre after automation releases propulsion)
notes: Modern automatics may coast or downshift; a single ICE value would be invented.

physical_meaning: deceleration produced by regenerative torque when the accelerator is released
powertrain_or_control_architecture: category A regen (not part of service brake), driver-selectable strength
measurement_method: on-road logging (S08, 4 EV models); dataset documentation (S26); regulation anticipates magnitudes via stop-lamp bands (S01)
reported_range: about 1 to 4 depending on regen setting; R13-H requires stop-lamp above 1.3 and allows it from 0.7
relevant_to_human_fallback: YES if automation releases the accelerator at TOR
notes: Mode-dependent (driver setting, state of charge, temperature, speed). The stop-lamp rule shows lift-off regen above 1.3 m/s2 is expected in practice, but gives no distribution.

physical_meaning: maximum deceleration available from the electric machine alone
measurement_method: dataset documentation and multi-EV testing (numeric values of S23 not retrieved)
reported_range: about 1 to 4 (0.1-0.3 g)
relevant_to_human_fallback: LIMITED (emergency braking exceeds regen capacity; friction brakes dominate)
notes: Bounded well below a_max; irrelevant to saturated emergency braking except through blending transients.

physical_meaning: deceleration commanded by partial / full accelerator release in one-pedal mode
powertrain_or_control_architecture: regen, sometimes blended with friction to standstill
reported_range: up to about 3 (≈0.3 g); torque peak 200-300 ms after lift-off (S08 citing Lee et al.)
relevant_to_human_fallback: YES (changes throttle-to-brake transition and brake timing, S22)
notes: Timing effect on the human (S22) is more relevant to fallback than the magnitude.

physical_meaning: fade of regenerative torque near standstill
reported_range: no numeric threshold or fade rate found
relevant_to_human_fallback: LOW (affects final metres of a stop)
notes: Code has v_rolloff parameters (R1 profile: 5 m/s, floor 0.2) that are COUNTERFACTUAL.

physical_meaning: time from brake command to onset of deceleration
powertrain_or_control_architecture: hydraulic friction brakes (S20, S04); any power-assisted service brake (S01)
measurement_method: instrumented tests (S20: 4 vehicles); regulatory response-time limit (S01); braking initiation time incl. pedal free travel (S04)
reported_range: hydraulic hard braking 0.05-0.17 (S20); pedal touch to deceleration 0.1-0.4 (S04); regulatory upper bound 0.6 to prescribed performance, incl. build-up (S01)
notes: S04 values include pedal free travel and human application speed. Brake-by-wire (V16) only bounded by the regulatory 0.6 s.

physical_meaning: time from deceleration onset to full / saturated deceleration
powertrain_or_control_architecture: hydraulic friction + ABS; brake assist where fitted
reported_range: time to 10 kg pedal force: professionals 0.05, non-professionals 0.83 (0.63-1.26 by car/condition); pedal touch to max depression 0.3-1.0; R157 benchmark driver 0.6 s 'jerking time to full deceleration' (Annex 3 Table 1)
notes: Build-up is dominated by how fast and firmly the human presses the pedal, not by hardware. A vehicle-only t3 is not identifiable from these sources.

physical_meaning: rate of change of deceleration during build-up
test_scenario: regulatory reference; comfort standard; naturalistic driving
reported_range: R157 benchmark 0.774 g in 0.6 s ≈ 12.65 m/s3 (Annex 3 Table 1); ACC about 2.5 (ISO 15622, SECONDARY ONLY); naturalistic non-emergency 99th pct about 2.6; human emergency jerk not measured
notes: Not an independent parameter once a_max and t3 are fixed.

physical_meaning: mean deceleration over an emergency stop with ABS on dry asphalt
vehicle_type: ABS passenger cars (2007-era, 2 models, S04); approval floor (S01)
measurement_method: instrumented trials; regulation; regulatory reference model
reported_range: professionals mean 8.4 (8.1-8.7); non-professionals 7.4 (6.6-8.7); 100-70 km/h interval about 9.1; approval floor 6.43 (R13-H Annex 3 §2.1.1); R157 benchmark 0.774 g ≈ 7.59 at road friction 1.0 (Annex 3 Table 1)
notes: Capability vs achieved deceleration must be separated: non-professional drivers achieved ~10% less on average, with large spread.

physical_meaning: mean deceleration over an emergency stop with ABS on wet asphalt
test_scenario: emergency stops on wetted sections (measured section friction 0.49-0.75)
reported_range: professionals 7.9; non-professionals 7.0
notes: Values are for clean wetted test sections; low-mu surfaces (snow, ice) not covered.

physical_meaning: tyre-road friction caps achievable deceleration
reported_range: a_max <= mu * 9.81
notes: The simulator carries road_friction but does not use it to cap a_max (code audit, R3A).

physical_meaning: fraction of available deceleration actually commanded by a human in an emergency
powertrain_or_control_architecture: human pedal input; brake assist where fitted
test_scenario: real intersection crashes (EDR, S05); test-track emergency stops (S04); simulator (S06)
reported_range: median average evasive braking 0.58 g ≈ 5.7 m/s2 in crashes (S05); non-professionals used about half the pedal force of professionals (S04); drivers brake fast but not firmly enough (S06)
relevant_to_human_fallback: YES (directly contradicts u = 1 as a behavioural assumption)
notes: Braking in the crash sample started late (0.5-1.5 s before impact) so average deceleration also reflects build-up; still well below capability.

physical_meaning: system that detects emergency braking from pedal force or speed and raises braking towards the maximum / ABS cycling
vehicle_type: passenger cars (UN framework: required with ESC)
powertrain_or_control_architecture: category A (pedal force) / category B (pedal speed)
reported_range: effect magnitude vehicle-specific; not quantified here
notes: Exists precisely because drivers under-apply the brake; activation thresholds are manufacturer-declared.

physical_meaning: command-to-pressure response of decoupled brake systems
measurement_method: no verified peer-reviewed numeric source retrieved
reported_range: upper bound 0.6 s to prescribed performance (regulatory, S01); commonly reported as faster than vacuum boosters (qualitative only)
relevant_to_human_fallback: LOW (sub-0.2 s effects are small relative to t1)
notes: Marketing figures deliberately excluded.

physical_meaning: hand-over between regenerative and friction braking during a stop or when demand exceeds regen capacity
powertrain_or_control_architecture: category B regen (part of service brake)
reported_range: blend curves proprietary; not published
notes: Product-specific; must not be claimed.

physical_meaning: deceleration and onset of AEB interventions
reported_range: manufacturer-dependent onset and deceleration (see literature matrix L011)
notes: Evidence that architectures differ; not transferable to human braking.

physical_meaning: available acceleration (relevant to merging / lane-change gap acceptance)
reported_range: EVs reach peak acceleration quickly and hold it (S08)
notes: Not needed for braking-only slice.

physical_meaning: deceleration / jerk limits of automation in normal operation
reported_range: ISO 15622 about 3.5 / 2.5 (SECONDARY ONLY); R157: system demand above 5.0 m/s2 is an emergency manoeuvre (§5.3.1.1)
relevant_to_human_fallback: YES (bounds automation-commanded a_pre during continued support)
notes: ISO values could not be verified: the public preview has no numeric limits.

physical_meaning: input-to-acceleration mapping of the D003 simulator vehicle
reported_range: unknown
notes: Owner question F1-F4; channel authorship B17.
